# Owned generic array and Object scalar fixture

A public static method receives an Object-bounded E array and an independent
Object key and returns an opaque int. A generic instance's private helper calls
it from an original T-array field before applying a boolean negative-result
policy. Source and SDK-provider profiles compile every recovered unit and retain
original entries, fields, flags, metadata and Exceptions.
Frozen direct, separately compiled, reflection and MethodHandle callers run
144 fresh JVM cases twice. They check exact array/key identity, aliases, cyclic
and covariant arrays, null/empty arrays, callback mutations, opaque integer
extremes and exact early/late failures. Element objects trap inspection.
Six wrong programs and six Code-preserving Signature controls guard the proof.
Only owned fixture code executes. Use JDK 25 for verification; originals compile
at release 8 and recovered sources use their reported Java release.

The `--seed-comparator` profiles add one method-owned value and a complete
contravariant Comparator input. Source and SDK modes compile all emitted Java,
compare every original definition and metadata value, and retain the existing
144-case matrix twice. Frozen direct, compiled, reflection and MethodHandle
callers also exercise both SDK binarySearch overloads with null/empty/covariant
arrays, insertion points, natural ordering and exact comparator exceptions.
Opaque owned providers must retain callback identity without inspecting or
invoking it. Eight independently compiled wrong programs and seven same-Code
Signature controls qualify these checks. Native controls cover alpha-renaming,
wide/range words, ignored results and rejection of open or unrelated seeds.
